text:
oliver: Heads-up — I'm running a set of Q4 capacity sims for embedding + rerank. Thinking about a 'split-pool scheduler' that can elastically move nodes between realtime and batch based on queue depth and tail latency. Need quick input on SLA targets + cost constraints by EOD.

sasha: quick q — how is this different from our current dedicated batch vs low-latency pools?

oliver: good q. Current model = hard split: separate pools, manual autoscale. The scheduler idea = logical pools with node assignment policy. nodes can be leased to batch when realtime idle, reclaimed on high tail latency. Benefit: better utilization, lower committed GPU hours. Risk: cache cold/warm churn, preemption jitter.

lee: sounds promising but region constraints bite. eu-west has ~20% less spare A100s in our quota window; moving nodes between roles cross-region is expensive (egress + longer reclaim times). If scheduler rebalances cross-region we pay egress and add 50-200ms reclaim. Need region-aware policy.

maria: also watch networking for rerank: typical rerank does a vector fetch + small model call. If vector store in another region that adds egress and suddenly spikes cost during rollouts. Simple formula I used for planning: cost_per_day = gpu_hours * gpu_rate + (egress_bytes / 1e9) * egress_rate. Plug in real numbers for Q4 sims.

ryan: product POV — our customer SLOs: 95p latency target for rerank should be <200ms for standard tier, <120ms for premium. If scheduler causes tail spikes above that we need fallback path (smaller model or cached responses).

ade: cache note — when nodes flip roles we lose local KV cache (prefix + rerank embedding caches). Cold starts add ~30-80ms depending on model. That undermines savings if churn > X transitions/hour. We should throttle reclaims with a cooldown window.

oliver: agreed. Proposed quick config snippet for scheduler policies:

```
policy:
  reclaim_thresholds:
    p95_latency_ms: 120
    queue_len: 300
  cooldown_minutes: 15
  region_awareness: true
  batch_spot_fallback: true
  max_cross_region_egress_gb: 50
```

lee: +1 to cooldown. For spot/backfill — prefer nightly batch jobs on preemptible in us-west and ap-south for cost, but only if preemption < 12% historically; otherwise fall back to dedicated pooled nodes.

maria: ops reminder — when doing dynamic leases we must export fine-grained tracing and token-level cost attribution (per-route). Otherwise billing + incident triage gets messy.

ops-bot: simulation job 1781234567-1 started (embed-rerank-scheduler-sim). ETA 2h. Logs -> https://internal.redwood/sim/1781234567-1

oliver: preliminary numbers from a 1h sim (single-region us-west, 4x A10g):
- baseline hard-split GPU hours/day: 960
- elastic split-scheduler estimate: 630 (34% reduction)
- added egress estimate/day if cross-region allowed: 120 GB -> ~$9/day at current rates
- tail latency p95 under policy: 138ms (with cooldown=15m), but cold-warm spikes to ~210ms when transitions happen rapidly

ryan: 34% is great, but premium customers won't tolerate p95 >120ms. Can we reserve a small dedicated buffer for premium queries (e.g., 10% capacity pinned)?

oliver: yep — plan to simulate pinned buffer = 10% dedicated + 90% elastic. Run that in next sim.

ade: also test 'cache affinity' — prefer keeping nodes assigned to rerank if they have warmed caches for top customers. Simple affinity label should help.

lee: action item — infra to provide region quota snapshots and spot preemption rates by tonight. I can also run a quick egress-cost sensitivity.

maria: ops will add tracing hooks and ensure per-request cost metrics are emitted for the sim.

oliver: thanks. Final asks from this thread:
1) product: confirm premium p95 target (ryan) — are we locking 120ms?
2) infra: region quotas + spot stats (lee)
3) sres: enable cost tracing for sim (maria)
4) eng: I'll run pinned-buffer sim and cache-affinity sim, post results in this thread.

sasha: pinging in case anyone has strong objections to the scheduler idea — I think ops complexity and visibility are biggest blockers.

oliver: no objections noted so far. If we get the data tonight we'll decide whether to run extended Q4 sims or proceed with a small pilot on a subset of customers next week. :eyes:
